scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

P-M2C.name: meter-to-cash
steps: read collection (AMI interval read or field manual read)
estimate substitution when no accepted read

DA-MDMS.name: MDMS AMI read event log (system of record for AMI reads)

DA-RULES.name: billing import validation rule change log

M-ESTIMATED-READ-SHARE.name: Share of disputed bills with ESTIMATED read type

F-01.statement: billing-db tariff_change_log contains zero records, indicating no tariff/rate change was logged.

F-02.statement: 1240 disputed bills had read_type ESTIMATED per billing-db disputed_bills_by_read_type.

F-03.statement: 1785 disputed bills had read_type ACTUAL per billing-db disputed_bills_by_read_type.

F-04.statement: route-log.route_completion_aug_sep shows manual-read route completion of 0.88 (target 0.95) covering 9200 manual read accounts for period 2026-08..09.

F-05.statement: crm-tickets dispute_response_times shows median 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days against a 3.0 day SLA across 2440 tickets.

F-06.statement: crm-tickets dispute_volume_monthly recorded 610 disputes (2026-06), 590 (2026-07), 1180 (2026-08), 1260 (2026-09), i.e. Aug-Sep roughly double the Jun-Jul baseline.

F-07.statement: Service contract §4.2 permits the utility to request field dispatch route priority changes, executed only after confirmation by the Field Operations Manager.

F-08.statement: route-log.lagging_routes returned 14 records with fields completion and route (14 distinct values each); sample record: completion=0.7, route=R-00.

F-09.statement: mdms-export read_events_for_disputed_estimated returned 2 records: 1184 with AMI read received before cutoff, exported_to_billing=true, billing_import_status=REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION; 56 with no AMI read received (NO_READ_RECEIVED), exported_to_billing=false.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-RESPONSE-HANDLING-GAP.statement: Dispute volume doubled because ticket response/handling is slow or inconsistent, not because bills are substantively wrong; an automated responder would close the gap.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August introduced incorrect handling of reads (e.g., estimate substitution or validation logic), producing wrong bills and the resulting dispute surge.

H-AMI-DELIVERY-FAILURE.statement: AMI/MDMS read delivery or validation (H-MDMS-BILL nightly export) degraded since August, causing billing to fall back to estimates or use bad reads, producing wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-FAILURE.statement: Manual field meter reads (H-FIELD-BILL daily upload from MeterWorks) became incomplete or late since August, forcing more estimated bills and triggering disputes.

H-LEGITIMATE-BILL-CHANGE.statement: Bills are substantively correct, but a legitimate change (e.g., tariff/rate or seasonal usage pattern) since August produced higher amounts that customers dispute even though no billing error exists.

H-AMI-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJECT.statement: Billing import validation rejects AMI reads flagged as high consumption and falls back to an estimate, producing ESTIMATED-read bills for AMI-metered accounts independent of field-reader staffing or route completion.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The billing-db tariff_change_log returned zero records, meaning no logged tariff/rate change occurred around the dispute surge period; this narrows H-LEGITIMATE-BILL-CHANGE to only the seasonal-usage-pattern variant, since a tariff-driven amount increase is ruled out.

billing-db's disputed_bills_by_read_type (E-02) shows 1785 disputed bills (59%) carry an ACTUAL read type and 1240 (41%) carry ESTIMATED, out of 3025 total disputed bills. This means estimate-substitution causes can at most account for a minority of disputed bills, while a majority of disputes involve bills that had a real (ACTUAL) read on file.

route-log shows manual field-read route completion for 9200 accounts was 0.88 against a 0.95 target over Aug-Sep 2026, i.e. a shortfall of roughly 7 points in completed manual meter-read routes during the dispute-surge window.

crm-tickets dispute_response_times (E-04) shows median 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days against a 3.0-day SLA across 2440 tickets, meaning ticket response handling is well within SLA rather than slow or inadequate as the initial request framed it.

E-05.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead, non-authoritative) claims there has been no tariff change this year, which agrees in direction with the already-recorded authoritative E-01 finding (billing-db tariff_change_log, 0 records, tariff_change_since_august=False). As a stakeholder statement it corroborates but does not independently establish the fact.

E-06.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD claims the field-reading team has been short three readers since July, causing routes to run late and those accounts to receive estimated bills instead of manual reads. This is a non-authoritative stakeholder claim offering a candidate mechanism for the route-completion shortfall already seen in E-03, not an independently verified fact.

crm-tickets dispute_volume_monthly (E-07) gives monthly dispute counts of 610 (2026-06), 590 (2026-07), 1180 (2026-08), 1260 (2026-09): Aug-Sep volumes are roughly double the Jun-Jul baseline, confirming the magnitude of the surge the initial request described, but it says nothing about why disputes rose.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Document E-08 (fieldco-service-contract §4.2) establishes that the utility may request field-dispatch route priority changes, but these are executed only after confirmation by the Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD); it is a process/authority artifact, not evidence about why disputes rose.

E-09.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log.lagging_routes (E-09) lists 14 routes with per-route completion values (sample: route R-00 completion=0.7), confirming individual lagging routes underlie the aggregate 0.88 completion rate (E-03). The record only contains fields completion and route — no staffing/reader-assignment field — so it cannot by itself verify whether the field-reader staffing shortfall (vs access, equipment, or scheduling causes) explains why these specific routes lag.

E-10.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI (non-authoritative) reports that MDMS export access for Lakeside has been provisioned as of today per vendor ticket TX-4471, which would remove the prior ACCESS_PENDING blocker on the mdms-export:read_events_for_disputed_estimated query; it says nothing about whether AMI delivery/validation itself actually degraded. Note runtime.tool_health still lists mdms-export as DEGRADED, so this access claim is unconfirmed and should be checked by attempting the query rather than accepted at face value.

mdms-export's read_events_for_disputed_estimated query (E-11) shows that of the disputed ESTIMATED-read bills (total 1184+56=1240, matching E-02's ESTIMATED count), 1184 (95.5%) had an AMI read received before cutoff and successfully exported to billing but rejected by billing import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, triggering estimate substitution; only 56 (4.5%) show no AMI read received at all. This indicates the dominant driver of ESTIMATED-bill disputes is a billing-side rejection of valid high-consumption AMI reads, not missing field/manual reads or AMI delivery failure.

U-AMI-DELIVERY-STATUS.question: Did AMI/MDMS read delivery or validation degrade since August, explaining the 59% of disputed bills that carry an ACTUAL read type?
U-AMI-DELIVERY-STATUS.decision_impact: Determines whether H-AMI-DELIVERY-FAILURE explains the majority of disputes, requiring a vendor-side remediation distinct from field-route fixes.
U-AMI-DELIVERY-STATUS.resolution_path: Obtain vendor-provisioned mdms-export access (currently DEGRADED/ACCESS_PENDING per the logged recovery decision) and query read_events_for_disputed_estimated.
U-AMI-DELIVERY-STATUS.safe_placeholder: Do not claim the field-staffing mechanism explains ACTUAL-read-type disputes; scope remediation to the ESTIMATED-read share only until resolved.

U-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.question: Did a billing import validation rule change around August (DA-RULES) introduce incorrect read handling contributing to disputes?
U-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.decision_impact: If confirmed, remediation shifts toward a billing-config fix rather than field staffing/route changes.
U-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.resolution_path: Query the billing-config rule change log for changes made around August 2026.
U-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.safe_placeholder: Treat H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE as open; neither confirm nor dismiss it in remediation scoping.

U-STAFFING-ROUTE-CAUSAL-LINK.question: Is the field-reader staffing shortfall the actual driver of the route-completion drop, or are there other causes (access, equipment, scheduling)?
U-STAFFING-ROUTE-CAUSAL-LINK.decision_impact: Affects whether remediation should specifically target headcount vs. other route-completion barriers.
U-STAFFING-ROUTE-CAUSAL-LINK.resolution_path: Obtain authoritative field-staffing records and correlate with route-log completion dates.
U-STAFFING-ROUTE-CAUSAL-LINK.safe_placeholder: Pursue generic route-completion remediation rather than committing to a headcount increase until corroborated.

U-ESTIMATED-BILL-ACCURACY.question: Are the ESTIMATED-read bills driving disputes actually inaccurate (billing error), or are correct estimates being disputed on perception/communication grounds?
U-ESTIMATED-BILL-ACCURACY.decision_impact: Determines whether restoring route completion alone resolves disputes or whether bill-accuracy/communication fixes are also needed.
U-ESTIMATED-BILL-ACCURACY.resolution_path: Cross-reference disputed ESTIMATED bills against later actual-read reconciliation amounts in billing-db.
U-ESTIMATED-BILL-ACCURACY.safe_placeholder: Treat estimate-driven disputes as a hypothesis; do not assume all require bill credits.
U-ESTIMATED-BILL-ACCURACY.resolution: For 1184/1240 disputed ESTIMATED bills, billing import rejected an actual high-consumption AMI read and substituted an estimate instead (E-11), indicating a substantive billing-accuracy issue (a real read overridden) rather than a perception/communication-only dispute for this majority of ESTIMATED cases.

A-STAFFING-CAUSES-ROUTE-SHORTF.statement: The field-reader staffing shortfall (SH-FIELD's claim, who has an incentive toward contract headcount increase) is assumed to be the actual cause of the measured route-completion drop, not merely a coincident claim.

A-ESTIMATED-BILLS-CAUSE-DISPUT.statement: ESTIMATED-read bills are assumed to be a driver of the disputes they are associated with, since E-02 shows association, not a verified causal link to billing errors.

A-DISPUTE-VOLUME-VALID-PROXY.statement: Monthly dispute ticket volume is assumed to be a valid proxy for bill correctness/customer satisfaction, even though volume could move for reasons unrelated to bill accuracy.

G-1.statement: dispute volume back to pre-August baseline with correct bills

K-BILLWRITE.description: Writes to customer bills (re-bill, credit) require Billing Operations authority; no automated bill writes.
